claim: In January 2026, Valor Equity Partners created a special purpose vehicle (SPV) named Valor Compute Infrastructure: a freestanding entity built to own hardware and raise debt against it, with no operating business of its own. Nvidia sold the vehicle more than 100,000 of its most advanced GB200 AI chips for roughly $5.4 billion and booked the full amount as revenue. Nvidia also invested about $1.9 billion of its own money into that same vehicle as sponsor equity. The chips physically run inside Elon Musk's xAI data center (the company behind the Grok chatbot), leased to an xAI subsidiary under a five-year triple-net lease; the vehicle's entire asset base is Nvidia GPUs leased to that single customer. Apollo Global Management arranged about $3.5 billion in debt for the structure, securitized it, and sold the resulting paper to Athene, Apollo's insurance subsidiary, which sells fixed and indexed annuities — contracts marketed to ordinary Americans as safe retirement savings. Investor Michael Burry, who profited shorting the 2008 subprime mortgage market, mapped the arrangement on his 'Cassandra Unchained' Substack on May 31, 2026 under the title 'The Retiree/Apollo/Nvidia/Bermuda/AMAPS/xAI Pipeline' and called it 'all Fugazi' — slang for fake. By Burry's reading of Athene's disclosures, the insurer has shifted roughly $217 billion of assets into a captive insurer in Bermuda, outside ordinary U.S. insurance regulation, with about 34.7 percent (~$103 billion) held as Level 3 assets — holdings with no observable market price, valued by the company's own internal models — leveraged roughly 16 times. Burry stresses that the steps are individually legal and disclosed and that he is not alleging fraud; his charge is that the architecture is engineered to move credit risk off balance sheets and onto annuity holders who did not knowingly take it on, echoing the off-balance-sheet packaging that preceded 2008. Nvidia rejects the characterization: in a memo to analysts that name-checked Burry, it said it does not use special purpose vehicles, does not rely on vendor financing, called 'circular financing' a mischaracterization because its strategic investments are a small fraction of revenue, and described its single disclosed guarantee as immaterial. Burry has maintained his analysis.

notes: Surfaced via capture DZs5nejzRzX (@natestav). The disclosed deal structure (Nvidia $5.4B GB200 sale to the Valor Compute Infrastructure SPV, $1.9B Nvidia sponsor equity, ~$3.5B Apollo debt securitized to Athene, GPUs leased to an xAI subsidiary) is verified against primary/strong-secondary reporting. The Bermuda captive figures ($217B moved offshore, 34.7%/~$103B Level 3, ~16x leverage) are Burry's own reading of Athene's disclosures and are attributed to him in the claim, not asserted in our voice — fits the 'separate primary fact from attributed conclusion' rule. Nvidia's analyst memo (CNBC, Nov 25 2025; reiterated for the Valor deal) denies SPV use and 'circular financing' and is cited for balance. Burry shut Scion Asset Management but kept publishing the 'Cassandra Unchained' / 'Heretic's Guide to AI's Stars' series. Sits alongside the off-balance-sheet SPV (2026-datacenter-offbalance-sheet-001), datacenter-bonds (2025-datacenter-bonds-yield-001), and hyperscaler-CDS (2026-hyperscaler-cds-001) records under the same anchor — the 2008-rhyme cluster.
